;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
**The [[Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons]] states it agrees with [[United Kingdom|UK]] authorities on their analysis of the identity of the toxic chemical used against the Skripals. The UK identifies the substance as a [[Novichok]] [[nerve agent]], of a type developed by Russia. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-43741140 (BBC)] [https://www.opcw.org/news/article/opcw-issues-report-on-technical-assistance-requested-by-the-united-kingdom/ (OPCW)]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**A further two [[Palestinian people|Palestinian]] protestors die, bringing the death toll at the [[Israel]]i-[[Gaza Strip|Gazan]] border to 34 since March 30. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/israeli-forces-kill-palestinians-gaza-protests-continue-180412175612461.html (al-Jazeera)]
**[[Adalah – The Legal Center for Arab Minority Rights in Israel|Adalah]] and [[Al Mezan]] say Gazan doctors had to amputate the legs of two young protestors wounded by Israeli fire after Israel refused permission for their transfer to [[Ramallah]] in the [[West Bank]] for treatment. Israel says the men were refused transfers because they were involved in violence. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/2-injured-gaza-protesters-said-to-lose-legs-after-access-to-west-bank-denied/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Egypt]], citing humanitarian reasons, opens the [[Rafah border crossing]] between Gaza and the Egyptian [[Sinai Peninsula]] for three days. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/egypt-opens-gaza-border-ahead-of-new-protests-against-israel/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**The 9th International Conference on the Holy City of Jerusalem begins, with Israel denying access to the [[Palestinian Authority]]-hosted conference to a number of foreign invitees including a party of thirteen [[India]]ns, two buses containing academics, and [[Ghana]]n MP [[Ras Mubarak]]. Israel's [[Ghana–Israel relations|ambassador to Ghana]] denies ever issuing Mubarak with permission to enter the [[Occupied Palestinian Territories]], calling Mubarak a "propaganda machine" and claims it's a "complete lie". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/jerusalem-conference-guests-denied-entry-israel-180412141116195.html (al-Jazeera)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Siege of Eastern Ghouta]]
***[[Syria]]n government fighters remove the last rebels from [[Douma, Syria|Douma]], completing the Syrian government's recapture of former rebel stronghold Eastern Ghouta. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/assad-government-forces-entire-eastern-ghouta-180412134000341.html (al-Jazeera)]
*[[Right-wing terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**The [[High Court of Justiciary|High Court]] in [[Glasgow]] sentences [[Banff, Aberdeenshire|Banff]] resident Connor Ward to life in prison with a minimum term of six years for plotting an [[Islamophobia|anti-Islamic]] terror attack against mosques in [[Aberdeen]]. [https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/news/aberdeenshire/1451904/banff-man-connor-ward-jailed-for-life-for-planning-terror-attacks-against-muslims/ (''The Press and Journal'')]
**Two serving soldiers are cleared of [[terrorism Acts|terror offences]] related to banned [[neo-Nazi]] group [[National Action (UK)|National Action]]. A civilian is convicted. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-43747111 (BBC)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-mid-wales-43756623 (BBC)] [https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/soldier-accused-recruiting-national-action-14411187 (''Birmingham Mail'')]
*Unidentified militants attack Kuru-kuru and Jarkuka in [[Zamfara]], [[Nigeria]], killing dozens. [https://punchng.com/bandits-attack-two-zamfara-villages-kill-scores/ (''The Punch'')]
*Ex-[[MI5]] agent [[Jeremy Fleming]] gives his first public speech as head of [[GCHQ]], revealing the [[United Kingdom]] launched a "major offensive cyber-campaign" against [[ISIL|Islamic State]]. He also criticises [[Russia]] for actions such as launching the [[NotPetya]] virus and the [[poisoning of Yulia and Sergei Skripal]], both actions Russia denies involvement in. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-43738953 (BBC)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Chernobyl disaster]]
**The [[Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant]] opens its doors to tourism. [http://tass.com/society/999300 (TASS)]
*[[Steve Huffman]], co-founder and CEO of [[Reddit]], says [[racism]] is allowed on the website. Some users criticize his position, while others praise Huffman for defending [[free speech]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-43738032 (BBC)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the United Kingdom]]
**Door-to-door sales firm [[Kleeneze]], which employs around 5,000 people, collapses into administration after 95 years. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-43746835 (BBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[List of shipwrecks in 2018|Shipwrecks in 2018]]
**The fire onboard [[South Korea]]n ship [[Fishing Vessel|FV]] ''Dong Won 701'' in the [[Timaru|Port of Timaru]], [[New Zealand]], enters its fourth day. The port resumes limited operations despite the ongoing blaze and the [[Transport Accident Investigation Commission]] starts an investigation despite being unable to board the vessel. [http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12030890 (''The New Zealand Herald'')] [https://www.stuff.co.nz/timaru-herald/news/103049279/fire-still-burning-but-port-resumes-some-operations (Stuff)]
*A [[Hellenic Air Force]] [[Mirage 2000-5F]] fighter jet crashes near the [[Greece|Greek]] island of [[Skyros]] in the [[Aegean Sea]] while intercepting a [[Turkey|Turkish]] aircraft that had violated Greek airspace. The pilot is reported dead. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/greece-fighter-jet-crash-missing-pilot-aegean-sea-turkey-skyros-mirage-a8301281.html (''The Independent'')] [http://en.protothema.gr/breaking-news-greek-military-airplane-goes-down-in-aegean-sea/ (Protothema)]
*Strong winds from a storm cause two of the [[Taj Mahal]]'s [[minarets]] to collapse. No injuries are reported [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-43735757 (BBC)]
*[[Tesla Inc.]] withdraws from the [[United States|U.S.]] [[National Transportation Safety Board]]'s probe of a fatal [[Tesla Model X|Model X]] crash in [[California]]. Tesla had drawn the NTSB's ire by releasing information publicly about its view of the case and about the car's Autopilot feature, something the Board does not allow during active investigations. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tesla-crash-autopilot/tesla-withdraws-as-party-to-ntsb-autopilot-crash-investigation-idUSKBN1HJ2JS (Reuters)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-04-12/tesla-withdraws-from-ntsb-crash-probe-over-autopilot-data-flap (Bloomberg)]

;International relations
*[[April 2018 inter-Korean summit|2018 inter-Korean summit]]
**A joint letter from more than 200 [[Non-government organization|NGO]]s urge [[South Korea]]n president [[Moon Jae-in]] to discuss [[North Korea]]n [[Human rights in North Korea|human rights]] at the April 27 summit. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/north-korea-human-rights-issues-summit-agenda-180412091005238.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[2018 Hamburg stabbing attack]]
**A man fatally stabs his ex-wife and his one-year-old daughter at a crowded subway platform in central Hamburg, Germany. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/2-dead-in-stabbing-at-hamburg-subway-station/2018/04/12/198b3b48-3e41-11e8-955b-7d2e19b79966_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Terrorism in Iraq]]
**Counterterror forces in [[Ninevah]] arrest and charge four suspected [[ISIL|Islamic State]] members over a fatal bombing at a market in regional capital [[Mosul]] last year. Separately, authorities discover an unidentified corpse in Mosul thought to be connected. [https://www.albawaba.com/news/iraqi-authorities-arrest-four-suspected-be-behind-mosul-terrorist-attack-1116496 (al-Bawaba News)]
**A mass grave containing burnt bodies is found in [[al-Tarabisha]], [[Al Anbar Governorate|Anbar]]. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/mass-grave-with-remains-of-burnt-bodies-found-north-of-ramadi-command/ (Iraqi News)]
*[[Stop Enabling Sex Traffickers Act]]
**[[Backpage]] CEO Carl Ferrer pleads guilty to conspiracy and money laundering and agrees to assist in the prosecution of other Backpage employees, including co-founders Michael Lacey and James Larkin, who were charged with several counts of human trafficking on April 6 after the site was seized by the FBI. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/backpage-com-ceo-plead-guilty-to-charges-1523579443 (''The Wall Street Journal'')] 

;Science and technology
* [[2018 in spaceflight]]
** [[NASA]] announces that the [[Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite]] will be launched from [[Cape Canaveral]] on April 16. [http://www.timesnownews.com/technology-science/article/nasas-next-planet-hunter-tess-spacecraft-launches-april-16/216519 (Times Now News)]
* [[2017 Atlantic hurricane season]]
** [[Hurricane Harvey|Harvey]], [[Hurricane Irma|Irma]], [[Hurricane Maria|Maria]], and [[Hurricane Nate|Nate]] join the list of [[List of retired Atlantic hurricane names|retired Atlantic hurricane names]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2018/04/12/hurricane-names-harvey-irma-and-maria-officially-retired/508363002/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[Threatened fauna of Australia]]
**The [[Mary River turtle]], which is endemic to the [[Mary River (Queensland)|Mary River]] in south-east [[Queensland]], [[Australia]], is added to the [[Zoological Society of London]]'s list of endangered species. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/12/asia/mary-river-turtle-endangered-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*A study in ''[[nature (journal)|Nature]]'' shows species which are visually unusual or [[attractiveness|attractive]] go extinct at higher rates. [http://www.techtimes.com/articles/224994/20180412/attractive-species-more-likely-to-go-extinct-study.htm (Tech Times)]
